subject: Maths
title: Applying Pythagoras in 2D problems
subtitle: Pythagoras' Theorem · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can apply Pythagoras' theorem to solve problems in 2D contexts.

key_vocab.definition: Pythagoras' theorem states a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse (longest side, opposite the right angle).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can apply Pythagoras' theorem to solve problems in 2D contexts.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Pythagoras' theorem -- Pythagoras' theorem states a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse (longest side, opposite the right angle).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Identify the right angle, label the hypotenuse (opposite it), then use a² + b² = c².
c = √(a² + b²)
Hypotenuse = square root of (sum of squares)

Key examples:
  ✓ Distance between (0,0) and (3,4) = √(9+16) = 5  (coordinate distance)
  ✓ Diagonal of rectangle 6 by 8 = √(36+64) = 10  (add squares)
  ✓ Ladder 5m, base 3m from wall: height = √(25−9) = 4m  (subtract)
  ✗ Diagonal of 6 by 8 rectangle = 6 + 8 = 14  (cannot just add sides)
  ✗ a² + b² = c² means a + b = c  (must square then root)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – coordinate distance
  Find the distance between A(1, 2) and B(4, 6).
  Horizontal distance: 4 − 1 = 3
  Vertical distance: 6 − 2 = 4
  Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5
  5 units
  (The distance formula is just Pythagoras applied to coordinates.)

Example 2 – diagonal of a rectangle
  Find the diagonal of a rectangle 5 cm by 12 cm.
  The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle
  d² = 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169
  d = √169 = 13 cm
  13 cm
  (The diagonal splits a rectangle into two right-angled triangles.)

sections.title: Coordinate distances
sections.content:
Find the distance between each pair of points.

(a) (0, 0) and (3, 4)
(b) (1, 2) and (5, 5)
(c) (0, 0) and (5, 12)
(d) (2, 1) and (6, 4)

sections.title: Diagonals
sections.content:
Find the diagonal of each rectangle.

(a) 3 cm by 4 cm
(b) 8 cm by 15 cm
(c) 7 cm by 24 cm
(d) 9 cm by 12 cm

sections.title: Ladder and ramp problems
sections.content:
Solve each real-life problem.

(a) Ladder 13 m, base 5 m from wall. Height?
(b) Ramp 5 m long, rises 3 m. Horizontal distance?
(c) Flagpole 12 m, wire anchor 5 m away. Wire length?
(d) Slide 15 m, height 9 m. Horizontal distance?

sections.title: Triangles and shapes
sections.content:
Find the unknown measurement.

(a) Isosceles triangle: base 8, equal sides 5. Height?
(b) Equilateral triangle side 6. Height?
(c) Square diagonal 10 cm. Side length?
(d) Rhombus diagonals 6 and 8. Side length?

sections.title: Mixed 2D problems
sections.content:
Answer each problem, giving answers to 1 d.p. where needed.

(a) Ship sails 8 km East then 6 km North. Direct distance?
(b) TV screen 40 cm by 30 cm. Diagonal?
(c) Kite string 25 m, horizontal distance 7 m. Height?
(d) Points (−2, 1) and (4, 9). Distance?
(e) Right triangle: legs 7 cm and 9 cm. Hypotenuse?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ The hypotenuse is always the longest side
✗ a² + b² = c means add and square root
✓ To find a shorter side, subtract the squares then square root
✗ Pythagoras works for all triangles
✓ The distance formula uses Pythagoras' theorem
